body:
I wonder if `std::array` wouldn't be more appropriate here. It's a little bit shorter since it guarantees always being full (so it doesn't have `_size`). It's not really important, but it might be an interesting question going forwards if we add more constants like this.

I'll probably bring this up in the next core meeting, and let you know if there is a consensus.

One of the two callers is using the given strings as `StringName`. I think it makes sense for this function to return `StringName`, since these are identifiers.

```suggestion
const Span<StringName> ScriptLanguage::get_core_type_words() const {
```

You'll also have to adjust each type word's constructor to run as `StringName("String", true)`, to mark them as static.
I thought the same. I don't know if `std::array` is allowed in our codebase. If it is ok I can change to use it.
I used to think the same, but I’m not sure which of the two callers is used more frequently. Considering that the conversion from `StringName` to `String` is very cheap, I think it is probably ok.
